question: A can do a piece of work in 32 days and B in 48 days. They work together for 8 days and then A goes away. In how much time (in days) will B finish the 60% of the remaining work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM of 32 and 48 = 96 units.

Efficiency of A = 3, Efficiency of B = 2 → Combined = 5 units/day.

Work done by A and B in 8 days = 8 × 5 = 40 units.

Remaining work = 96 − 40 = 56 units.

Time required for B to finish 60% of remaining work = (56 × 60/100) ÷ 2 = 33.6 ÷ 2 = 16.8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 32 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 48 days

A and B worked together for 8 days.

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 32
 96
 3
 
 

 B
 48
 2
 
 

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 8 days = 8 × 5 = 40 units

⇒ Remaining work = 96 − 40 = 56 units

⇒ 60% of the remaining work = (60 / 100) × 56 = 33.6 units

⇒ Time taken by B to complete this 60% work = Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B = 33.6 ÷ 2 = 16.8 days

⇒ 16.8 days = 16 ⁸/₁₀ days = 16 ⁴/₅ days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Time & Work

Assuming the total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual days makes the calculations fraction-free. The efficiency is simply Total Work ÷ Number of Days.

Work & Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. A highly efficient person will take less time to finish the work. Work done = Efficiency × Time.

Leaving Mid-way Problems

Calculate the total work completed during the combined working period, subtract it from the total assumed work, and assign the remainder entirely to the remaining active workers.
